purpose: The originality half of the IP programme had never produced a number. The screening tool was written and correct and had never run against anything - status CORPUS_REQUIRED, blocker APPROVED_OFFLINE_EXTERNAL_CORPUS_NOT_PROVIDED - so 'is the protected core original' stood unmeasured while being read as unfavourable. One corpus needs no approval and no network: the dependencies this repository already has on disk, which is also the likeliest way third-party code reaches a first-party module by accident. The first commit on this branch screened against an npm-only corpus and reported 688 files clean; 151 of the 688 are Python and the npm store holds one .py file, so 22% of the core had been compared against an effectively empty set. The corpus now carries the Python roots the interpreter itself reports plus the declared apps/tai closure, and the record states per-language coverage, names the 28 files no corpus covers, and publishes the negative falsification result. No verdict is claimed and no ASVS decision is touched.
requiredInvariants: The screening tool is not modified. Its normalisation, fingerprints, thresholds and refusals are exactly as they were; this branch supplies a corpus it can read and records what came back.

The corpus is rebuildable rather than shipped. Nothing under node_modules and nothing from the interpreter is committed, the builder hard-links so the corpus costs no additional space, and the record carries the aggregate digest so a rerun can be compared against this one.

Every corpus root is flattened to one path segment. The screening tool excludes any path containing a node_modules, dist, build, test or fixture segment - correctly, or it would scan our own installed tree and call our dependencies our own code - and pnpm stores packages at .pnpm/<id>/node_modules/<name> while /usr/lib/python3.11/distutils/tests is three excluded segments at once. Pointed at either directly the run would report a clean result over an empty corpus, which is the most dangerous possible outcome because it looks like proof. The suite asserts this for both npm and Python names.

A corpus is evidence only for the languages it contains, and the builder prints its own composition by extension on every run so that cannot be assumed again. The record states per-language coverage and names the 28 files - 24 SQL against a corpus with no SQL, 4 stylesheets against 26 - that this run does not cover.

A clean result is not reported until the run is shown capable of a dirty one, in every language claimed. Verbatim and comment-stripped copies of a TypeScript file and a Python file were planted in the protected core and all four were caught.

A falsification stage that fails is published as a failure. A verbatim 1838-line copy with every non-keyword identifier renamed is not detected by any of the three methods, so the record says that 'no findings' means 'no copy that survives reformatting' and not 'nothing was copied'.

The three findings are classified by measurement, not by reading them. Two barrels contain zero characters once re-export lines and comments are removed; the Python file contains zero executable statements by ast.parse. The classification is mechanical in all three cases.

The record corrects its own predecessor in its own text rather than replacing it silently: it states what the first run said, what was overstated, that coverage rather than the verdict was wrong, and that the error came out of the run's numbers rather than out of review.

The record states its own limits: nothing about the unscreened files, nothing about a corpus outside our own dependencies, nothing about a renamed copy, and nothing about authorship, which is a separate claim with separate evidence and remains blocked on four owner documents.
acceptance: 688 protected files screened against 25 478 corpus files drawn from 1146 npm packages and 6 Python roots; corpus digest 360ca182428c88bef3a4b312589a7a0bf3518ee417933da2525d527d8d91e041; 87 findings; exactly 3 source files affected; 0 substantive.
All three affected files measure zero - zero characters of non-re-export code for the two barrels, zero executable statements for apps/tai/tai/__init__.py - so the classification is mechanical.

Per-language coverage is published: .ts 456 files against 7919, .py 151 against 2393, .tsx 53 against 10 .tsx but 1061 JSX-bearing corpus files across 57 React-family packages, .sql 24 against 0, .css 4 against 26. 660 files screened, 28 declared unscreened.

Falsification stage 1: verbatim copies of zod/src/v3/types.ts (5138 lines) and pydantic/main.py (1838 lines) planted in the protected core are caught as EXACT_SHA256. Stage 2: both with comments stripped are caught as NORMALIZED_TOKENS. Stage 3: both with every non-keyword identifier renamed are not detected, and the record publishes that. All stages on the same corpus and settings that report the core clean; the planted files were removed and the tree restored.
The corpus rebuilds reproducibly from one command: 1146 packages, 6 of 6 Python roots, 75 778 regular files, 4 non-regular entries dropped, no additional disk used, composition printed by extension.

build-dependency-corpus.test.mjs passes 8 of 8, including that neither an npm entry name nor a Python root name can contain an excluded path segment, that a symlinked package directory is not counted as a package, and that an interpreter which cannot be probed yields nothing rather than throwing. Both new invariants were verified by mutation: breaking the flattening and breaking the root filter each fail exactly one test.
No ASVS decision, no verdict and no application code is touched; the matrix is unchanged against main.
